text:
Potash has been found beneath the Hadrow Flats, according to the Hadrow Basin Survey Consortium, which announced the discovery on 14 March 2024.

The findings are set out in the consortium's "Hadrow Flats Preliminary Assessment Report," presented at the Northern Mineral Resources Forum. Core samples indicated a potash-bearing seam roughly 42 meters thick, with an estimated 310 million tonnes of recoverable deposit, the report states.

Dr. Imelda Corvane, the consortium's lead geologist, presented the assessment. The document describes the work as preliminary, and it does not set out a timetable for further drilling or for any commercial development of the site.

Potash is a potassium-rich mineral used chiefly in agricultural fertiliser. The report's figures rest on core samples taken at the survey site and have not been independently reviewed in the material presented at the forum.
